cards.title: Linear conditional information for proper agnostic VC learning
cards.formal: Conjecture 6 of the cited paper asks whether there is a universal constant c>0 such that, for every binary class H of VC dimension d≥1 and every n≥d, a randomized proper learner A:(X×{0,1})^n→H has CMI_D(A)≤cd for every distribution D and E_A[loss(A(z),z)]≤inf_{h∈H}loss(h,z)+c√(d/n) for every sample z. The intended arbitrary-domain measurable-space convention remains to be specified; this is not yet a completed benchmark statement.
cards.why: Tests whether proper agnostic VC learning can attain near-best empirical accuracy while retaining only O(d) bits of information about the sample-selection experiment. This separates a property of the learner from the power of a generalization-bound technique.
cards.status_note: Source and subsequent-work check on 11 September 2026 found no resolution of Conjecture 6 in the stated proper agnostic setting. The 2020 realizable-case refutation and chained-information analysis have different guarantees. The arbitrary-domain measurable model remains unspecified, so current openness and complete benchmark formulation are not certified.

cards.definitions: H is a nonempty set of functions X→{0,1}; a finite subset B⊆X is shattered when all its binary labelings are restrictions of functions in H. Its VC dimension is the maximum shattered cardinality. Proper means that every output belongs to H. For z=((x_i,y_i))_{i=1}^n, loss(h,z)=(1/n)Σ_i 1[h(x_i)≠y_i]. To define CMI_D, draw a supersample Z̃=(Z̃_i,0,Z̃_i,1)_{i=1}^n with 2n independent draws from D, and independent fair bits S=(S₁,…,S_n); feed the selected sample (Z̃_i,S_i)_i to A with independent randomness. Put W=A((Z̃_i,S_i)_i). CMI_D(A)=I(W;S|Z̃)=H(S|Z̃)−H(S|W,Z̃), with base-two conditional Shannon entropy of the finite random variable S. The learner may depend on H,n, but not on D. The source does not specify sigma algebras for arbitrary X,H, measurability of evaluation, or admissibility of learners and distributions; those choices affect the quantified statement. No domain restriction is silently added here.

sentences: Conditional mutual information measures what a learner’s output reveals about which examples were selected from an independent supersample.
The target is the proper agnostic-learning Conjecture 6 of Steinke and Zakynthinou: information O(d) and expected empirical excess loss O(√(d/n)).
Here d is the VC dimension, n is sample size, and the learner must work for every data distribution.
The paper’s separate proper realizable Conjectures 7 and 8 were refuted by Haghifam, Dziugaite, Moran and Roy in 2020.
Measurability conventions for the arbitrary-domain question remain to be specified, so this formulation is still marked unfinished.

context_blocks.text: A learner can fit its observed labels while retaining information that is irrelevant to future prediction. Conditional mutual information measures one aspect of this dependence: after revealing a pool of two candidate examples for each position, how much does the output reveal about which member of each pair was actually used? The hidden selection consists of n fair bits, so this information is between zero and n bits. The conjecture asks whether dependence can be limited by the class complexity d while retaining near-best training accuracy.

For a one-pair illustration, fix two different candidate observations. An output that identifies the selected observation reveals the selector bit completely; an output independent of that choice reveals nothing. This describes the information experiment, not a proposed learning algorithm. The conditioning removes uncertainty about the observations themselves, so even an observation with an arbitrarily long numerical description need not reveal more than that one selection bit.

Agnostic means that observed labels need not agree with any hypothesis in the class. The empirical comparison is therefore with the best in-class training loss, rather than with zero. Properness requires the output to remain in that same class. The learner may vary with the class and sample size but must be chosen before the data distribution; otherwise the distribution-free claim changes.

The source gives an empirical-risk minimizer with CMI at most d log n+2. Its question is whether the logarithmic dependence on sample size can be removed if expected empirical excess loss of order √(d/n) is allowed. The significance is that the ordinary CMI generalization inequality would then recover a dimension-dependent √(d/n) scale without an extra logarithmic loss.

The paper’s Conjectures 7 and 8 instead ask for proper realizable learners with expected empirical loss O(d/n), or zero. Haghifam, Dziugaite, Moran and Roy refute those claims in Theorem 4.2. Their negative theorem assumes that sharper empirical-loss requirement. Since d/n can be much smaller than √(d/n), it cannot simply be substituted for a refutation of the agnostic Conjecture 6 retained here.

Hafez-Kolahi and coauthors recover tighter VC generalization estimates through chained conditional mutual information. This shows that an information-theoretic analysis can eliminate the extra logarithmic factor by changing the bound being analyzed. It does not supply a proper learner whose unmodified output CMI obeys the conjectured O(d) bound. A statement about a successful analysis and a statement about how much information the learner itself retains are different.

One formulation issue remains explicit. On arbitrary domains, the probability distributions, hypothesis-valued random output and evaluation map require compatible measurable structures. Those conventions are not specified in the cited conjecture. This card preserves that gap instead of silently restricting the question to a finite domain. Its content and source distinction have been improved, but it is still an unfinished benchmark formulation.

methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large groups of 50 and 25 small groups of 20: 1000 planned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. Top 100 and Top 1000 use the first 5/2 and 50/20 category places respectively. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
